title: The Parable of the Two Eagles and the Vine
description: Ezekiel tells a mysterious parable about a great eagle that takes the top of a cedar from Lebanon and plants it in a trading land, where it becomes a vine. The vine turns toward another great eagle to be watered, but the prophet explains that this means the king of Babylon took Judah's king and made a covenant with him, while the king broke the covenant by seeking help from Egypt. The Lord proclaims judgment over the breach of covenant, but concludes with the promise that he himself will take a twig from the top of the cedar and plant it on Israel's high mountain, so that it may become a mighty cedar where all birds can dwell.
